schemaClass.name: Action
schemaClass.description: An Action entity specifies the mechanism by which inputs are transformed into outputs.

schemaProperty.name: Percent Complete
schemaProperty.description: Percent Complete represents the percentage this Action is complete.

schemaProperty.name: Start
schemaProperty.description: Start represents the time when this Action begins.

schemaProperty.name: Duration
schemaProperty.description: Duration represents the period of time this Action occurs.

schemaClass.name: Artifact
schemaClass.description: An Artifact entity specifies a document or other source of information that is referenced by or generated in the knowledgebase.

schemaProperty.name: Date Published
schemaProperty.description: Date Published represents the date when this Artifact was accessed (webpage), published, or uploaded to the knowledgebase.

schemaProperty.name: File
schemaProperty.description: The File that represents this Artifact.

schemaClass.name: Asset
schemaClass.description: An Asset entity specifies an object, person, or organization that performs Actions, such as a system, subsystem, component, or element.

schemaClass.name: Resource
schemaClass.description: A Resource entity specifies a consumable or producible Asset.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Resource's units used to measure the amounts, such as each or tons.

schemaProperty.name: Initial Amount
schemaProperty.description: Initial Amount represents this Resource's starting amount.

schemaProperty.name: Minimum Amount
schemaProperty.description: Minimum Amount represents this Resource's minimum amount allowed.

schemaProperty.name: Maximum Amount
schemaProperty.description: Maximum Amount represents this Resource's maximum amount allowed.

schemaClass.name: Port
schemaClass.description: An interaction point of a block, specifying the input and output flow.

schemaProperty.name: Direction
schemaProperty.description: Direction represents the flow of data on this port.

schemaClass.name: Characteristic
schemaClass.description: A Characteristic entity specifies properties of an entity.

schemaProperty.name: Value
schemaProperty.description: Value represents this Characteristic's current value.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Characteristic's units used to measure the value, such as pounds or miles per hour.

schemaClass.name: Measure
schemaClass.description: A Measure entity specifies properties of measurements and measuring methodologies, including metrics.

schemaProperty.name: Projected Value
schemaProperty.description: Projected Value represents this Measure's expected value to be achieved with existing resources.

schemaProperty.name: Threshold Value
schemaProperty.description: Threshold Value represents the minimum acceptable value for this Measure.

schemaProperty.name: Objective Value
schemaProperty.description: Objective Value represents the goal for this Measure.

schemaProperty.name: Improvement Direction
schemaProperty.description: Improvement Direction represents the direction in that metric improvement occurs. It is the direction from the Threshold Value to the Objective Value.

schemaProperty.name: Tolerance
schemaProperty.description: Tolerance represents the percentage of the value that forms the positive and negative tolerance bands. Tolerance is used when Value represents the planned measure value at a given time.

schemaClass.name: Connection
schemaClass.description: A Connection entity specifies the mechanism relating Assets. This is an abstract class.

schemaClass.name: Conduit
schemaClass.description: A Conduit entity specifies the connection between Assets and has capacity and latency, which carries an Input/Output.

schemaProperty.name: Capacity
schemaProperty.description: Capacity represents the maximum rate supported by the Conduit. (Used in simulation as to add time delay by dividing the Input/Output size with the capacity value.)

schemaProperty.name: Latency
schemaProperty.description: Latency represents the time required to transmit the information or Input/Output entity over this Conduit. This value does not factor in any delays due to capacity limitations.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Conduit's units used to measure the capacity, such as bits per second or gallons per minute.

schemaClass.name: Logical
schemaClass.description: A Logical entity specifies relationship between Assets. It is primarily used in database schema development and entity-relationship diagrams.

schemaClass.name: Cost
schemaClass.description: A Cost entity specifies the outlay or expenditure (as of effort or sacrifice) made to achieve an objective associated with another entity.

schemaProperty.name: Amount
schemaProperty.description: Amount represents this Cost's value.

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Cost's units used to measure the amount, such as $ or Euro.

schemaProperty.name: Rate
schemaProperty.description: Rate represents this Cost's billing rate.

schemaProperty.name: Category
schemaProperty.description: Category represents the part of the lifecycle for which the money is used (commonly called Color of Money). This matches the Federal Government (DoD) cost phases.

schemaProperty.name: Contract Type
schemaProperty.description: Contract Type represents this Cost way to identify the reimbursement structure (i.e. CPFF vs T&M).

schemaClass.name: Decision
schemaClass.description: A Decision entity specifies a challenge and its resolution.

schemaProperty.name: Justification
schemaProperty.description: Justification represents the reason and context for making this Decision.

schemaProperty.name: Assumptions
schemaProperty.description: Assumptions represents facts that are used as a basis for this Decision. These assumptions can be taken for granted by the decision maker.

schemaClass.name: Equation
schemaClass.description: An Equation entity specifies an equation (mathematical or logical) that can be used to describe a part of the model.

schemaProperty.name: Value
schemaProperty.description: Value represents this Equation's text.

schemaClass.name: Input/Output
schemaClass.description: An Input/Output entity specifies the information, data, or object input to, triggers, or output from an Action.

schemaProperty.name: Size
schemaProperty.description: Size represents the amount or proportion of this Input/Output, such as 100 as in 100 Gigabytes or number of entities (e.g. 10 as in 10 tokens).

schemaProperty.name: Units
schemaProperty.description: Units represents this Input/Output's units used to measure the size, such as Gigabyte or tokens.

schemaClass.name: Issue
schemaClass.description: An Issue entity specifies a bug, user story, or an epic.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Issue.

schemaProperty.name: Assignee
schemaProperty.description: Assignee represents the user(s) and/or team(s) responsible for the issue.

schemaProperty.name: Priority
schemaProperty.description: Priority represents the level of effect this issue is causing.

schemaClass.name: Location
schemaClass.description: A Location entity specifies where an entity resides.

schemaClass.name: Orbital
schemaClass.description: An Orbital entity specifies a location along an orbit around a celestial body.

schemaProperty.name: Apoapsis
schemaProperty.description: Apoapsis represents the point of greatest distance from the celestial body being orbited. For Earth, the term is apogee. For the Sun the term commonly used is aphelion. The Apoapsis must be specified with the Periapsis to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Periapsis
schemaProperty.description: Periapsis represents the point of closest distance from the celestial body being orbited. For Earth, the term is perigee. For the Sun the term commonly used is perihelion. The Periapsis must be specified with the Apoapsis to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Eccentricity
schemaProperty.description: Eccentricity represents the amount the orbit deviates from a perfect circle (0 being perfectly circular and 1 is a parabola - no longer a closed orbit). The Eccentricity must be specified with the Semimajor axis to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Semimajor Axis
schemaProperty.description: Semimajor Axis represents the one half of the length of the longest diameter of the orbital ellipse. The Semimajor axis must be specified with the Eccentricity to characterize the orbital ellipse shape.

schemaProperty.name: Inclination
schemaProperty.description: Inclination represents the angle between the orbital plane and a reference plane, such as the equatorial plane for Earth. The Inclination must be specified with the Longitude of Ascending Node to characterize the orbital plane.

schemaProperty.name: Reference Plane
schemaProperty.description: Reference Plane represents the reference plane from where the Inclination angle will be calculated.

schemaProperty.name: Longitude of Ascending Node
schemaProperty.description: Longitude of Ascending Node represents the angle from the Origin of Longitude to the ascending node, measured in the Reference Plane. For the Earth, the origin of longitude is typically the Prime Meridian. The Longitude of Ascending Node must be specified with the Inclination to characterize the orbital plane.

schemaProperty.name: Origin of Longitude
schemaProperty.description: Origin of Longitude represents the reference meridian from where the Longitude of Ascending Node will be calculated.

schemaProperty.name: Argument of Periapsis
schemaProperty.description: Argument of Periapsis represents the angle between the Periapsis and the ascending node as measured in the orbital plane in the direction of motion.

schemaProperty.name: Mean Anomaly
schemaProperty.description: Mean Anomaly represents the proportion of orbital area swept since the last Periapsis at the specified time. It is used to define the position of the orbiting Asset along the orbital ellipse.

schemaClass.name: Physical
schemaClass.description: A Physical entity specifies a location on or above the surface.

schemaProperty.name: Address
schemaProperty.description: Address represents this Location's complete address.

schemaProperty.name: Coordinates
schemaProperty.description: Coordinates represents the coordinate points for this Location (GPS or other system).

schemaProperty.name: Altitude
schemaProperty.description: Altitude represents the distance above the surface.

schemaClass.name: Virtual
schemaClass.description: A Virtual entity specifies a location within a digital network.

schemaProperty.name: Address
schemaProperty.description: Address represents the identification address using the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) protocols.

schemaClass.name: Risk
schemaClass.description: A Risk entity specifies the combined probability and consequence in achieving objectives.

schemaProperty.name: Consequence Description
schemaProperty.description: Consequence Description represents the result of this Risk occurring.

schemaProperty.name: Consequence
schemaProperty.description: Consequence represents the level of effect from this Risk occurring.

schemaProperty.name: Probability
schemaProperty.description: Probability represents the chance that this Risk will occur.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Risk.

schemaClass.name: Statement
schemaClass.description: A Statement entity specifies text referenced by the knowledgebase and usually contain in an Artifact.

schemaClass.name: Requirement
schemaClass.description: A Requirement entity identifies a capability, characteristic, or quality factor of a system that must exist for the system to have value and utility to the user.

schemaProperty.name: Rationale
schemaProperty.description: Rationale provides a place to capture the reason(s) behind this Requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Quality Score
schemaProperty.description: The calculated quality score.

schemaProperty.name: Appropriate
schemaProperty.description: Appropriate represents if this Requirement expresses the specific intent and amount of detail of the need or requirement statement appropriate to the level (the level of abstraction, organization, or system architecture) of the entity to which it refers.

schemaProperty.name: Complete
schemaProperty.description: Complete represents if this Requirement sufficiently describes the necessary capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor to meet the need, source, or parent requirement from which it was transformed without needing other information to understand the requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Conforming
schemaProperty.description: Conforming represents if the Requirement is conforming to an approved standard pattern and style guide or standard for writing and managing needs and requirements.

schemaProperty.name: Correct
schemaProperty.description: Correct represents if this Requirement is an accurate representation of the need, source, or parent requirement from which it was transformed.

schemaProperty.name: Feasible
schemaProperty.description: Feasible represents if this Requirement can be realized within entity constraints with acceptable risk.

schemaProperty.name: Necessary
schemaProperty.description: Necessary represents if this Requirement defines an essential capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor needed to satisfy a lifecycle concept, need, source, or parent requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Verifiable
schemaProperty.description: Verifiable represents if this Requirement is provable (within realistic cost and schedule) that the system meets the requirement.

schemaProperty.name: Singular
schemaProperty.description: Singular represents if this Requirement states a single capability, characteristic, constraint, or quality factor.

schemaProperty.name: Unambiguous
schemaProperty.description: Unambiguous represents if this Requirement is stated such that the requirement can be interpreted in only one way by all the intended stakeholders.

schemaClass.name: Time
schemaClass.description: A Time entity specifies a point or period when something occurs or during which an action, asset, process, or condition exists or continues.

schemaProperty.name: Start
schemaProperty.description: Start represents the time when this Time begins.

schemaProperty.name: Duration
schemaProperty.description: Duration represents the period of time this Time occurs.

schemaClass.name: Test Case
schemaClass.description: A Test Case entity represents a set of conditions utilized to determine whether a system works as intended.

schemaProperty.name: Set Up
schemaProperty.description: Set Up represents the prerequisites that must be fulfilled before executing this Test Case.

schemaProperty.name: Expected Result
schemaProperty.description: Expected Result represents the result expected when executing this Test Case.

schemaProperty.name: Actual Result
schemaProperty.description: Actual Results represents the results that are captured after executing a Test Case.

schemaProperty.name: Status
schemaProperty.description: Status represents the current state of this Test Case.

schemaClass.name: Task
schemaClass.description: A Task entity specifies an Action that must be completed for a particular project. It served as a "To-Do" for the Project.

schemaClass.name: Dependency
schemaClass.description: A Dependency entity specifies a connection between two Tasks in a Gantt Chart. It defines the relationship a Task depends on another Task in order to Start or Finish

schemaClass.name: Transition
schemaClass.description: A Transition entity specifies an action that, once completed, transitions one state (Characteristic) to another state (Characteristic).

schemaRelation.name: alternative
schemaRelation.description: Alternative identifies the Statement that is a potential choice for this Decision.

schemaProperty.name: Choice
schemaProperty.description: Choice represents if this alternative was the choice selected.

schemaRelation.name: alternative of
schemaRelation.description: Alternative of identifies the Decision that has this Statement as a potential choice.

schemaProperty.name: Choice
schemaProperty.description: Choice represents if this alternative was the choice selected.

schemaRelation.name: caused by
schemaRelation.description: Caused by identifies the entity that this Issue/Risk results.

schemaRelation.name: causes
schemaRelation.description: Causes identifies the Issue/Risk resulting from this entity.

schemaRelation.description: Connected by identifies the Connector that adjoins this Asset.

schemaProperty.description: Origin represents if the Asset is the origin of the Connector. This attribute enables unidirectional (one or the other Asset's relationship origin is False), in additional to the default bi-directional flow (both origins are set to True as a default).

schemaProperty.name: Multiplicity
schemaProperty.description: Multiplicity represents if this connection has multiple connections to the Asset.

schemaRelation.name: connects to
schemaRelation.description: Connects to identifies the Asset that this Connector adjoins.

label.name: Independent Verification & Validation Plan Document
label.description: Independent approach to verification and validation (IV&V) Plan documents the approach and processes that will be used to ensure that an independent approach to the verification and validation is incorporated into the project from the beginning of the lifecycle through implementation.

label.name: Test Plan Document
label.description: The Test Plan document documents and tracks the necessary information required to effectively define the approach to be used in the testing of the project's product.

label.name: Integrated Logistics Support Plan Document
label.description: The Integrated Logistics Support Plan (ILSP) serves as the master logistics planning document that describes necessary logistic activities, assigns responsibility for those activities, and establishes a schedule for completion.

label.name: Standard Operating Procedure Document
label.description: A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is a set of step by step instructions for carrying out a specific technique. They can be used for any technique, but this guide focuses on their use in documenting monitoring techniques, specifically for species and ecological communities.

label.name: Concept of Operations Document
label.description: The Concept of Operations Document (CONOPS) is both an analysis and a formal document that describes how an asset, system, or capability will be employed and supported.

label.name: Requirements Document
label.description: The Requirements Document provides the stakeholders with a clear statement of the capabilities required of the system in order to solve the stakeholder's needs.

label.name: Simulation Output
label.description: Is the dashboard from an executed simulation.

label.name: Project Management Plan Document
label.description: The Project Management Plan (PMP) is a formal document used to document planning assumptions and decisions, facilitate communication among staekholders, and document approved scope, cost, and schedule baslines.

label.name: Final State
label.description: A UML State Machine's final state.

label.name: Initial State
label.description: A UML State Machine's initial state.

label.name: Report
label.description: System generated reports contain this label.

entity.name: Report program participation
entity.description: I need to see how many people enrolled and how often they log during the pilot, so I can show the program's value to my committee.

entity.name: Pilot Sponsor / Administrator
entity.description: Buyer and program operator. Power 8.2/10, interest 8.0/10: Players - Manage closely. Priority rank 2 of 7.

entity.name: Compare against a fair baseline
entity.description: I need the always-drive comparison to use the same distance and a stated vehicle factor and occupancy, so the comparison is fair.

entity.name: Log my commute quickly
entity.description: I need to record my daily commute in a few seconds, because I will not keep using something that adds work to my morning.

entity.name: Minimise personal data
entity.description: I need the product to keep only the location detail it needs, so a leaked record reveals as little as possible.

entity.name: exclude infeasible modes
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall exclude from its recommendations every travel mode that the Commuter has marked as not feasible.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Prevents advice the Commuter has already ruled out, such as cycling with equipment or when carrying children. MOE: Number of recommendations that include a mode marked not feasible (target 0) MOE selection: A zero-defect count shows directly whether the Commuter's own limits are respected. Validation: Rule test set covering every combination of marked-not-feasible modes; pass if no recommendation contains an excluded mode. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.1.4 (BMA N4)

entity.name: Method Reviewer Needs
entity.description: Needs voiced by Sustainability and Transportation Staff (Method Reviewers) (SH.4).

entity.name: Protect Personal Data and Consent
entity.description: Collect, store, restrict and delete personal data under consent and minimisation rules.

entity.name: recommend a feasible lower-emission option
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall provide, for each accepted trip with an eligible lower-emission option, one alternative travel mode with a stated reason based on trip distance, forecast weather and the Commuter's feasibility settings.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Advice only changes behaviour if it fits the Commuter's situation; a stated reason lets the Commuter judge it. MOE: Percentage of surveyed Commuters who rate the advice feasible (target 80% or more) MOE selection: Feasibility as perceived by the Commuter is the outcome the stakeholder cares about; rule firing counts would not show it. Validation: Post-result survey in the pilot; report opt-outs and non-response; rule review against the product description rule (distance under 3 km and no rain). Verification method: Demonstration Source needs: 1.1.4 (BMA N4)

entity.name: disclose estimation method
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall display, with each trip result, the emission factor source, the factor version and the distance convention used to calculate it.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: People trust an estimate only if they can see what it rests on; also supports reviewer traceability. MOE: Percentage of displayed trip results that carry source, version and distance convention (target 100%) MOE selection: A completeness count is objective and directly reflects the stakeholder's need to know where numbers come from. Validation: Inspection of a random sample of 50 displayed results in the pilot build; pass if every sampled result shows all three items. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.1.3 (BMA N3, N6)

entity.name: calculate a declared baseline
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall calculate the always-drive baseline from the trip distance, a declared vehicle emission factor and a declared occupancy.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: A baseline is fair only if its assumptions are stated and applied consistently. MOE: Percentage of audited trips whose baseline matches the declared assumptions (target 100%) MOE selection: A fidelity check shows whether the baseline does what it claims. Validation: Recalculate the baseline for a sample of 50 trips and compare with system output. Verification method: Analysis Source needs: 1.4.2 (BMA N6)

entity.name: Commuters
entity.description: Primary users. Power 7.0/10, interest 9.3/10: Players - Manage closely. Priority rank 3 of 7.

entity.name: Keep my trips private
entity.description: I need to decide who can see my trip records and be able to remove them, so I feel safe sharing my routine.

entity.name: Get consent before storing trips
entity.description: I need each person's consent recorded before any trip is stored, so we can show that participation was voluntary.

entity.name: Operate Service
entity.description: Keep the web service available and sized for the pilot cohort.

entity.name: Get advice I can use
entity.description: I need suggestions for a greener way to travel that fit the weather and my own limits, so I get advice I can actually follow.

entity.name: Review Commute Impact and Feasible Alternative

entity.name: conform to accessibility standard
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA for the commute entry and result views.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Inclusive access is a charter expectation and a pilot-entry condition. MOE: Number of unresolved WCAG 2.2 Level AA failures in the entry and result views (target 0) MOE selection: Standard conformance gives an externally recognised, countable result. Validation: Accessibility audit of both views plus keyboard and assistive-technology tasks; pass if no failures remain open. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.1.7, 1.5.3 (BMA N8)

entity.name: explain result from calculated facts
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall display with each trip result a plain-language explanation that states only facts contained in the calculated result: the estimated CO2e, the baseline difference, the factor source and version, and the recommendation reason.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Commuters read a result more easily in words, but unsupported generated text would reduce trust and could overclaim savings (BMA risk R8); the explanation may only restate calculated, rule-approved facts and must not calculate emissions, invent weather or override eligibility rules. MOE: Number of sampled explanations that contain a figure, weather condition or travel mode not present in the calculated result (target 0) MOE selection: A zero-defect count of unsupported statements directly shows whether the explanation stays inside the calculated result. Validation: Inspect a random sample of 50 displayed explanations in the pilot build, comparing each field by field with the calculated result; pass if none contains an unsupported figure, condition or mode. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.1.8 (BMA N3)

entity.name: stay within the baseline cost
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall cost no more than $750,000 to develop and deploy.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: The baseline budget in the project charter limits the investment the Company Sponsor has approved. MOE: Cost variance against the $750,000 baseline (target 0% or less) MOE selection: Variance from the approved baseline is what the sponsor tracks at each gate. Validation: Sponsor reviews cost forecast, scope variance and evidence at each stage gate. Verification method: Analysis Source needs: 1.3.1 (BMA N10)

entity.name: Evaluate Pilot Performance
entity.description: Record usage events and report pilot results against the measures of effectiveness.

entity.name: store only coarse location
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall store trip location only at coarse-area granularity.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Precise coordinates are unnecessary for the product and increase harm if records leak. MOE: Number of stored records that contain precise coordinates (target 0) MOE selection: A zero count shows that minimisation is working. Validation: Database inspection on the pilot build and a field-level data review. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.5.1 (BMA N7)

entity.name: Retire the service cleanly
entity.description: I need to shut the service down without leaving personal data behind, so we do not carry liability after the program ends.

entity.name: Commuter Needs
entity.description: Needs voiced by Commuters (Students and Employees) (SH.1).

entity.name: Retire Service
entity.description: Delete identifiable records and export approved aggregates when the service is retired.

entity.name: Avoid overclaiming savings
entity.description: I need savings shown as estimates rather than verified avoided emissions, so program reports do not overclaim.

entity.name: label differences as estimates
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall label each baseline difference as an estimated difference.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: The difference is a modeled counterfactual, not verified avoided emissions. MOE: Percentage of displayed baseline differences labelled as estimated (target 100%) MOE selection: A labelling count shows whether the product avoids overclaiming. Validation: Inspection of all views that show a baseline difference. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.4.3 (BMA N6)

entity.name: enable fast trip entry
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall enable a Commuter to submit a commute log entry in 30 seconds or less for at least 80 percent of timed entry tasks.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Entry effort is the main barrier to repeated self-reporting; the target is the existing product target in the BMA (80% under 30 seconds). MOE: Percentage of timed entry tasks completed in 30 seconds or less (target 80% or more) MOE selection: It measures the effort the Commuter actually experiences, which is an effectiveness measure; internal response time would only measure the system. Validation: Pilot usability session: at least 20 participants each log five trips on their own device; time from entry form ready to entry accepted; pass if 80% or more of tasks take 30 seconds or less. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.1.1 (BMA N1)

entity.name: Enabling Providers
entity.description: Suppliers. Power 2.4/10, interest 2.2/10: Crowd - Monitor with minimum effort. Priority rank 7 of 7.

entity.name: report pilot results
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall provide the Company Sponsor with pilot results for each stakeholder measure of effectiveness before June 30, 2027.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: The launch decision is scheduled for June 30, 2027 and needs evidence first. MOE: Number of measures of effectiveness with reported pilot results at the decision date (target equal to the number defined) MOE selection: It checks that the evidence the sponsor needs actually arrives in time. Validation: Evaluation report checked against the MOE list at the launch-decision gate. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.3.2 (BMA N10)

entity.name: operate with the pilot cohort
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall operate without functional failure with at least 500 enrolled Commuter accounts.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: 500 enrolled users is the existing pilot participation target in the BMA and must be technically possible. MOE: Number of enrolled Commuter accounts with which the system operates without functional failure (target 500 or more) MOE selection: Cohort size is the sponsor's direct indicator of pilot scale. Validation: Create 500 test accounts and run the entry and summary tasks; pass if no functional failures occur. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.3.2 (BMA N2)

entity.name: delete trip records on request
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall permanently delete all of a Commuter's trip records upon the Commuter's deletion request.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Control over one's own data builds the trust needed for voluntary participation. MOE: Percentage of deletion requests that leave no identifiable trip record (target 100%) MOE selection: Completeness of deletion is what the Commuter can rely on; it is objectively countable. Validation: Deletion test: create records for test accounts, request deletion, query storage and backups in scope; pass if none remain. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.1.6 (BMA N7)

entity.name: record consent before storing trips
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall require a recorded Commuter consent before storing the first trip record.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Shows that participation is voluntary and informed. MOE: Number of stored trip records without prior recorded consent (target 0) MOE selection: A count of exceptions is what the assurance reviewers need for sign-off. Validation: Test flow: attempt to store a trip without consent and with consent; audit stored records against the consent log. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.5.2 (BMA N7)

entity.name: Get pilot evidence for the launch decision
entity.description: I need measured results on participation and use before the launch decision, so I can decide whether to invest further.

entity.name: Company Sponsor
entity.description: Acquirer. Power 9.2/10, interest 7.2/10: Players - Manage closely. Priority rank 1 of 7.

entity.name: record accepted-log events
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall record a timestamped event for every accepted trip log so that weekly active use can be computed for each enrolled Commuter.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: The launch decision depends on engagement evidence, which can only be computed if usage events are recorded. MOE: Percentage of enrolled Commuters whose weekly active status can be computed from recorded events (target 100%) MOE selection: Completeness of the evidence base is what the sponsor needs before relying on the engagement figure. Validation: Reconcile the event log with accepted entries for test accounts; pass if every accepted entry has exactly one event. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.3.2 (BMA N2, N10)

entity.name: Know where the numbers come from
entity.description: I need to know where the numbers come from and what they leave out, so I can trust them.

entity.name: Stakeholder Needs
entity.description: Stakeholder needs of the major stakeholders of the EcoCommute system, expressed as the stakeholders would state them.

entity.name: reproduce reference cases
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall reproduce each agreed reference-case CO2e result to the nearest gram.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Reference cases give an independent check on the calculation, including units and occupancy handling. MOE: Percentage of agreed reference cases reproduced (target 100%) MOE selection: It compares the system with calculations the reviewers made independently. Validation: Reviewers calculate the reference cases independently and compare with system output. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.4.1 (BMA N6)

entity.name: suppress small groups
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall suppress any aggregate group that contains fewer than 5 Commuters.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Small groups can be re-identified from aggregates. The value 5 is a proposed default because the BMA leaves the threshold open; the pilot sponsor must confirm it. MOE: Number of reported groups with fewer than 5 Commuters (target 0) MOE selection: It converts re-identification risk into a countable, testable measure. Validation: Aggregation test with seeded groups of sizes 1 to 10; pass if no group below the threshold is reported; sponsor confirms threshold. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.2.2 (BMA N7)

entity.name: use reviewed emission factors
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall calculate trip CO2e using only reviewed emission factors that record source, units, geography and version.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Traceable factors make results defensible and allow later review. MOE: Percentage of calculated trips whose factor record is complete (target 100%) MOE selection: Provenance completeness is what the Method Reviewer needs to defend a number. Validation: Audit of factor store and a sample of calculated trips; confirm source, units, geography and version are present. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.4.1 (BMA N6)

entity.name: delete identifiable records at retirement
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall permanently delete all identifiable Commuter records at service retirement.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Prevents the company from carrying personal data after the program ends. MOE: Percentage of identifiable Commuter records deleted at retirement (target 100%) MOE selection: Completeness of deletion is the sponsor's liability measure. Validation: Disposal rehearsal on a copy of the pilot data before retirement; sponsor-approved retention review. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.3.4 (BMA N12)

entity.name: Trace every number to a source
entity.description: I need every CO2 estimate to trace to a published emission factor with its source, units and version, so I can defend the number to others.

entity.name: Pilot Sponsor and Administrator Requirements
entity.description: Stakeholder requirements derived from the needs of Institutional Pilot Sponsor and Administrator (SH.2).

entity.name: pass assistive-technology walkthrough
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall allow a keyboard-only user and a screen-reader user to complete the commute entry task before pilot readiness.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Verifies accessibility with real tasks before real users are enrolled. MOE: Number of unresolved critical task barriers for keyboard and screen-reader users (target 0) MOE selection: Task completion shows whether conformance on paper translates into real access. Validation: Moderated walkthrough with at least one keyboard-only and one screen-reader user; barriers logged and resolved. Verification method: Demonstration Source needs: 1.5.3 (BMA N8)

entity.name: Provide Approved Aggregate Summary
entity.description: Institutional reporting scenario: aggregate summary for the Pilot Administrator (BMA Section 7.1 notes it as a separate scenario).

entity.name: Keep the service running
entity.description: I need the service to be available when participants try to log, so they keep the habit and I keep their trust.

entity.name: Use it without barriers
entity.description: I need to use the application with my phone, keyboard or screen reader, so everyone in my group can take part.

entity.name: Understand my result in plain words
entity.description: I need a short plain-language explanation of my trip result and the suggested alternative, so I understand what the numbers mean and can decide for myself.

entity.name: Verify accessibility before the pilot
entity.description: I need keyboard and screen-reader checks passed before the pilot starts, so no one is excluded from day one.

entity.name: Stakeholders
entity.description: All stakeholders identified in the Power-Interest Grid analysis (Stakeholder Needs and Requirements Definition).

entity.name: Web Front End
entity.description: Internal asset of C.0 EcoCommute (Web Front End); see docs/context.md in the TEAM-6 repository.

entity.name: Application Service
entity.description: Internal asset of C.0 EcoCommute (Application Service); see docs/context.md in the TEAM-6 repository.

entity.name: Data Adapter
entity.description: Internal asset of C.0 EcoCommute (Data Adapter); see docs/context.md in the TEAM-6 repository.

entity.name: Explanation Model
entity.description: Internal asset of C.0 EcoCommute (Explanation Model); see docs/context.md in the TEAM-6 repository.

entity.name: restrict access to individual trip records
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall restrict access to each Commuter's individual trip records to that Commuter.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Privacy control is a condition of participation for Commuters and a legal and reputational risk for the sponsors. MOE: Number of individual trip records exposed to any other role in access tests (target 0) MOE selection: A single exposure defeats the purpose, so the measure is a count that must stay at zero. Validation: Role-based access test matrix across Commuter, Pilot Administrator and company staff roles; residual privacy-risk review by the assurance reviewers. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.1.6, 1.2.2 (BMA N7)

entity.name: Company Sponsor Requirements
entity.description: Stakeholder requirements derived from the needs of Company Sponsor and Leadership (SH.3).

entity.name: Protect individuals in reports
entity.description: I need summaries that never reveal one person's trips, so participants and my office stay out of a privacy dispute.

entity.name: provide participation summary
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall provide an authorized Pilot Administrator with the enrollment count, the weekly active count and the total CO2e for a selected reporting period.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: The sponsor needs engagement evidence for its own reporting; these three figures are the minimum the BMA identifies. MOE: Percentage of the sponsor's reporting questions that the summary answers or explicitly defers (target 100%) MOE selection: It tests the summary against what the sponsor actually has to report rather than against what the system happens to produce. Validation: Review the approved summary against the sponsor's list of reporting questions at pilot readiness; record deferrals with sponsor agreement. Verification method: Demonstration Source needs: 1.2.1 (BMA N5)

entity.name: Method Reviewers
entity.description: Method credibility. Power 5.6/10, interest 5.9/10: Players - Manage closely. Priority rank 4 of 7.

entity.name: See what my trip emitted
entity.description: I need to see how much CO2 my trip produced and how it compares with driving alone, so I know what my choice meant.

entity.name: display trip impact and baseline difference
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall display the estimated CO2e of each accepted trip, in grams, together with its difference from the always-drive baseline within 3 seconds of entry submission.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Immediate, connected feedback is the core value proposition. The 3-second limit is a proposed responsiveness threshold to confirm in discovery. MOE: Percentage of surveyed Commuters who correctly explain the estimate and the baseline difference (target 80% or more) MOE selection: Comprehension, not mere display, shows whether the feedback is useful to the Commuter. Validation: Structured comprehension questions after use in the pilot; disclose sample size and scoring; confirm display time with a timing test on three reference devices. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.1.2 (BMA N3)

entity.name: exclude individual data from summaries
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall exclude individual Commuter identifiers and trip records from every institutional summary.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Institutions should see program-level evidence only, which keeps individual privacy and limits the sponsor's exposure. MOE: Number of individual identifiers or trip records found in institutional outputs (target 0) MOE selection: Any single occurrence is a privacy failure, so a zero-count measure is appropriate. Validation: Output inspection and access tests on every summary type before release. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.2.2 (BMA N5, N7)

entity.name: Track my progress
entity.description: I need to see my weekly and monthly totals and my savings against driving, so I can tell whether my habits are improving.

entity.name: Keep the scope under control
entity.description: I need the product kept to manual logging and coarse location unless I approve a change, so cost and privacy exposure do not grow quietly.

entity.name: Deliver Pilot Release
entity.description: Develop and deploy the baseline release inside the approved budget.

entity.name: export approved aggregates at retirement
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall export the approved aggregate summaries at service retirement.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Preserves program evidence for the institution without keeping personal data. MOE: Percentage of approved aggregate summaries exported at retirement (target 100%) MOE selection: A completeness count shows that the evidence the institution is entitled to survives closure. Validation: Disposal rehearsal verifies the export file against the approved summary list. Verification method: Test Source needs: 1.3.4 (BMA N12)

entity.name: Stakeholder Requirements
entity.description: Stakeholder requirements of the EcoCommute system, each derived from one or more stakeholder needs.

entity.name: Engineering and Support
entity.description: Build and support. Power 3.2/10, interest 8.4/10: Subjects - Keep informed. Priority rank 6 of 7.

entity.name: maintain service availability
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall maintain an availability of at least 99.5 percent during each month of the pilot.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Reliable access protects the logging habit and the sponsor's credibility; the value is the existing product target. MOE: Measured monthly availability (target 99.5% or more) MOE selection: Availability as experienced by users is the usual effectiveness measure for dependable service. Validation: Define the measurement period and exclusions before the pilot; monitor a successful service check every minute; report monthly. Verification method: Analysis Source needs: 1.2.3 (BMA N9)

entity.name: Assurance Reviewers
entity.description: Assurance. Power 7.4/10, interest 4.3/10: Context Setters - Keep satisfied. Priority rank 5 of 7.

entity.name: avoid device location traces
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall not collect location traces from Commuter devices.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Passive GPS is excluded from the baseline scope; collecting it would raise cost and privacy exposure. MOE: Number of device location traces collected (target 0) MOE selection: A zero count shows directly that the scope boundary is respected. Validation: Network and storage inspection of the pilot build; pass if no location traces are transmitted or stored. Verification method: Inspection Source needs: 1.3.3 (BMA N10)

entity.name: Pilot Sponsor and Administrator Needs
entity.description: Needs voiced by Institutional Pilot Sponsor and Administrator (SH.2).

entity.name: display trends and cumulative difference
entity.description: The EcoCommute system shall display each Commuter's weekly and monthly CO2e totals and cumulative CO2e difference from the always-drive baseline.

stringAttribute.value: Rationale: Seeing progress over time is what keeps a Commuter logging after the first week. MOE: Weekly active use after eight weeks (target 40% or more of enrolled Commuters) MOE selection: Sustained use is the best available proxy for the Commuter finding the trend feedback worthwhile; it is the existing BMA target. Validation: Cohort report: a Commuter is active if there is at least one accepted log in the preceding seven days; denominator is all enrolled Commuters; measured at week eight. Verification method: Analysis Source needs: 1.1.5 (BMA N2)
